id:
Swaggering Rooster, one of the celestial creatures competing in Emperor Yu's search for a trusted assistant, was eager to show off her martial prowess in a world without warfare. With her flair for showiness and the right amount of intimidation, Kelsa was admitted into the blood-soaked underbelly of the concrete jungle. A veritable den of vicious villainy...and yet, an opportunity to sharpen long-dulled spurs.

It came as no surprise that a woman named after a particular breed of bruisers would be anything less than a runaway hit in the ring. After a stunning first bout which left her opponent blacked out on the floor, the match offers came pouring in. Kelsa took it all in stride. Back in Heaven such violence was reserved only for times of great peril, but the last war was several hundred years ago over a miscreant of a monkey. It was long past time to get cracking.

While her hulking competition prioritized brute, overwhelming strength, Kelsa took advantage of her natural agility and discerning eye for weak spots, sealing her wins with a decisive heel drop. Sure, these aren't the villains she was accustomed to dealing with, but humbling hubristic humans made for quite the rush. Better yet, no one had to die.

Throughout her fast-rising "career", Kelsa came to know of another celestial presence in the city, though Snake (who now called herself Rhyne) preferred not to draw blood in her own performances. The two still hang out to this day; there would certainly be quite a turnout should the two pull off an aggressive routine on stage...or holding their own against one of the many opponents Kelsa has publicly humiliated.

id:
Deep within the frigid forests of the Frozen Mountains, the Northern Isengrim tribe of wulfs roam their snowy home in service and protection of the divine spirit known as Forest Mother. Appearing as little more than children with wolfish features, these proud warriors take their legacy seriously, for they are the descendants of the White Wulf God, Fenrir. As such, it is a tribal tradition for even young pups to undertake hunts on their own, to better prove their might and eligibility to become the next White Wulf of their tribe—a title befitting only the most heroic warrior of a hundred years.

Now, the time has come for one stout-hearted pup to shine. Though only a juvenile, nothing scares the brave wulf Faelan; not the bitter cold of the endless blizzard, nor the howling snowstorms that threaten to lay great pines low. No, she will hunt the beast of the frozen lake and claim its head, and surely the village will recognize her as the next White Wulf!

Armed with her fishing rod and her hand-carved hook, the young pup heads off for the hunt of her lifetime, unaware of what fate had in store for her that day. After all, no one sets out expecting to deal with very different sorts of beasts in a decidedly un-snowy locale. Who would have thought that strange, shimmering portal was more than a curiosity and would take her to a dense jungle with abundant—and delicious—prey?

Nevertheless, the beast in the frozen lake back home could certainly wait in its silty slumber. For now, there was the matter of getting home—along with a strange, snivelling little cat-girl with horns she'd stumbled upon...

id:
Far and away in the arid deserts of Baldemar live the Morokai, a proud and fearsome race of horned humanoids. Though danger is rife in the badlands and capable adults often travel long distances to hunt, their children are given free rein to navigate the world around them, honing valuable survival skills for a rough life ahead. It is here, on a particularly blazing summer day, that a mischievous little Morokai girl grows restless for adventure—when big sister Nyala is away, little sister Nyami finds her chance to play!

With her trusty new spade, bucket, and a generous supply of pudding in tow, Nyami sets out for the oasis at the entrance of the badlands. A nice, cooling dip in azure waters, topped off with delicious, creamy dessert, would be the perfect cure to the sizzling summer heat. And what's more, surely she can find new, sparkly treasures to add to her little stash—all before Nyala gets home! Nyala never did like when her little sister headed out, but it was just a short trip. Who would find out?

As she reached her little emerald getaway, Nyami's ears pricked in excitement as the lake called out to her. She was getting dreadfully sticky from the journey, and a running leap straight into paradise was in order.

But when Nyami emerged from the pool, the oasis was no more. For one, a jungle this dense was unheard of in such an unforgiving landscape; and for two, the lake had swelled immensely beyond its tiny boundaries, culminating in a velvety stretch of soft sand unlike the harsh desert.

Quietly gathering up her equipment, the little Morokai girl squirms. Perhaps now was a good time to go home to big sister Nyala...

id:
"Though its scent lingers, the flower's form has long since scattered. Such is the transience of life; such is ephemeral beauty."

So were the words of strange wisdom from a stranger, forgotten land. Sages and fools alike pondered the passage of time, each inevitably concluding that indeed, everything is temporary. A gentle, wistful melancholy pervaded their world and was rooted in their hearts; even a shattered vase was all the more beautiful for its cracks, lacquered in liquid gold.

The gods of their land, known as kami, were symbolic of such transient cycles. As forces of nature, they were simultaneously fleeting and omnipresent: like the flash of lightning or the swirl of incense smoke. Given form, they were beings and took names; yet among them was a human of such extraordinary circumstance that he was counted among their ranks.

None can say who or what the ascended kami Suizen was in life, only that while his flesh was fragile, his spirit was not. He etched his being not only in the roar of thunder, but in the echoing silence that followed. Despite his fearsome symbolism, Suizen is polite and demure, and is said intervene in affairs far more than any other.

Not long after, a trickster slipped among the faithful—a centuries-old fox, whose cruel wiles displaced an elderly priest and fooled the followers. Suizen confronted the beast and vanquished him, quenching his ambition forever; neither hide nor hair was seen of the fox thereafter, but the shroud over the land that followed in his wake seemed to portend worse.

It would take a slow spiraling end for the two to meet again—but this time, among the ashes of a sunken past beneath the absent moon.

"Though its scent lingers, the flower's form has long since scattered. Such is the transience of life; such is ephemeral beauty."

So were the words of strange wisdom from a stranger, forgotten land. Sages and fools alike pondered the passage of time, each inevitably concluding that indeed, everything is temporary. A gentle, wistful melancholy pervaded their world and was rooted in their hearts; even a shattered vase was all the more beautiful for its cracks, lacquered in liquid gold.

The gods of their land, known as kami, were symbolic of such transient cycles. As forces of nature, they were simultaneously fleeting and omnipresent: like the flash of lightning or the swirl of incense smoke. Given form, they were beings and took names; yet among them was a human of such extraordinary circumstance that he was counted among their ranks.

None can say who or what the ascended kami Suizen was in life, only that while his flesh was fragile, his spirit was not. He etched his being not only in the roar of thunder, but in the echoing silence that followed. id:
Out of the twelve celestial creatures of Heaven, Dog seemed best suited for the job of being Emperor Yu's trusted assistant. No one could be more loyal and patient than he was, but out of fairness (and perhaps the Emperor's entertainment), a competition was drawn up with a level playing field in the realm of the humans. Dog readily agreed; after years in paradise, it was time to revisit his old roots and prove that his faithful nature to mortal masters had not changed one bit since his ascension.

Gone were the rice fields and countryside cottages of centuries past. In their place rose monoliths of concrete and glass, with sputtering streetlamps that cast lonely shadows. It seemed to Dog that, more than ever, his kind was needed as a protective presence.

His first attempts at greeting a human were met with wariness. Perhaps it was his antiquated speech or the manner of his courtly dress, which he insisted on retaining upon his arrival. It was soon apparent that he would have to adjust to new preferences, should he wish to continue his guardianship.

In recent nights, rumors abound of a strange young man and his oddly canine get-up. Some complain of the malaise shared by youths of the current generation, and others worry that he is a thief, a ruffian, or worse. But for the "Black Dog", as the local press called him, seeing drunk or solitary humans safely through the night and to their homes is enough for him.

Besides, the more plucky of the youths he sees home has already befriended him. As far as they were concerned, Kirke was now a member of their pack.

id:
Stick around the alleys at midnight long enough, and you're bound to run into a masked young man perched atop a wire fence. Without another word, he'll follow you around from a distance, but he never seems to be in the vicinity when you look. Kirke has become something of an urban legend in the city, but as long as the celestial dog was able to satisfy his protective streak, he was more than happy to be a ghost.

One of the contenders in Emperor Yu's competition in search for the perfect assistant (a role many believed he was already qualified for), Kirke did as his nature commanded: become a worthy companion and protector of humans, as he did in the days before his ascension. But the new world had shed its old ways, and it was getting increasingly difficult to convince any human of his good intentions in the traditional fashion.

Not to be dissuaded, Kirke donned a new coat and collar and called upon the zeitgeist—brooding, dark, and melancholy creatures skulking away from the light. He blended in seamlessly with the local youth, even sparking interest among patrons of a nearby underground club. Kirke would soon learn that the celestial Dragon—now named Noxa—was their local celebrity. She was amused to see him stalk into her den with several of her regulars, but nevertheless welcomed him to the sleepless city.

Having found a place in his new pack, Kirke delights in safeguarding his young charges. His youthful appearance belied centuries of guardianship, and many a bully or thug has broken speed records escaping from his shadowy hounds.

After all, Kirke was not one for words; his bite was far, far worse than his bark.

id:
Crown Prince Gortius, though eldest son of King Radmuhl and next in line for the Elysian throne, much preferred running drills in the courtyard with his men than debate nobles in court. Where his younger sister Estia studied the comforting mystique of the Light, Gortius spent his formative years chasing dreams of gallant heroism.

Upon his twenty-fifth summer, Gortius personally mounted a bold offensive against the Northern pirates. Though the Northern Campaign was a resounding success, it was said to have cost Gortius his life, forever lost beneath the waves. All Elysia mourned their Crown Prince, but none was more aggrieved than his father—the sorrow of which would eventually claim the old king's life.

In truth, Gortius had secretly fled from the burdens of eventual kingship with Miriam, his half-Alethi second in command. The frozen steppes of Eiros served as the backdrop of their idyllic life for some five winters—as well as the birthplace of their daughter, Evgenia.

Fate would soon catch up with the prince, however, when troubles at home forced Gortius to return to Elysia. Reasonably just toward friend and foe alike, Gortius's kindness was a liability in the mire of his court, a shortcoming that Miriam was eager to compensate with lethal judgement. As much as Gortius loved his family, the stresses of rulership caught up with them, forever changing the once-happy family—and culminating in his quiet demise.

Though detractors declare him the end of House Valen, others agree Gortius's spirit still lives on in Evgenia, whose burning resolve shines through her defiant eyes and carries the torch of her father for the long years ahead.

Where his younger sister Estia studied the comforting mystique of the Light, Gortius spent his formative years chasing dreams of gallant heroism.

Upon his twenty-fifth summer, Gortius personally mounted a bold offensive against the Northern pirates. Though the Northern Campaign was a resounding success, it was said to have cost Gortius his life, forever lost beneath the waves. id:
Children of the snow-driven steppes, Kyria and her two elder brothers possessed an intrinsic sense for life on a saddle—an advantage for those who live by the frontiers. Their lowborn status availed them little except the livelihood of herders, but the local lord saw in her brothers budding cavalrymen, and conscripted them into his service.

Life was harsh, but it was nothing compared to the terrible darkness that swept over the steppes. The winged, malicious terror came by cover of night, and the people burned in its wake. So fierce and suffocating were the flames from its maw that ash was all that remained of its unfortunate victims. With each dawn came the dread realization that no one would save them; least of all their absent lord and his cavalry.

But Kyria did not give up. One night, after the beast had slaked its thirst for carnage, she quietly saddled up her family's last stallion and tracked it. Through the valley of death she dared—then two radiant strangers clad in shining armor came riding out of the brume, raising a hand in greeting. Fearful yet enraptured, Kyria followed in silence.

Strewn all over the lair were the broken bodies of the brave and the foolish. The strangers inclined their helmeted heads before a single broken lance jutting defiantly toward the heavens, then vanished. Kyria stifled a cry as she spied her beloved brothers' eagle-talon necklaces among the mangled corpses.

As dawn began to break, Kyria's resolve grew, and a chorus of phantom voices urged the rider on—their instrument of justice. The dragon would draw its final noxious breath, and every one of these brave souls would be avenged. For Kyria, it would be a good death...

id:
One of the Seven Demonlords of Nogreth, and leader of the "Chilling Beauties." Hilda is originally from Phillarm and her partner in crime is a large snake.

Blaming the King for the death of her beloved father, she began following Elhaza, who fed her grudge against him. She coldly carried out any missions given to her as a member of the Nogreth forces, including trifling with a certain group of young knights. However, upon discovering the real cause of her father's death she was overcome by emotion, and following her younger sister's lead, chose to protect the knights against Melfel instead. She was then vanished to another world after sacrificing herself to save the others.

id:
One of the Seven Demonlords of Nogreth, and Hilda's younger sister. A free spirit, she does whatever she pleases wherever she pleases, and her partners in crime are ice spirits.

After receiving the tragic news of her father's death, she stayed by Hilda's side to support her despite the rage that had overcome her older sister. Upon becoming a member of the Nogreth forces, she is forced to fight against a certain group of knights against her will. However, she values her relationships with others above everything else, and it is this characteristic that eventually helps her win over the heart of the Summoner. Ironically, after losing both her father and her sister, the only friends she has left are her former enemies.

id: A war general from a world in turmoil that came to be known as the "Little Conqueror." After inheriting his father's great legacy at a young age, he used his own great might to befriend other powerful military generals, adding their forces to his ranks and expanding his influence even further. Said to be a very handsome and open-minded man, he charmed many who were elated to enter his service. His drive to build the foundations of his nation was such that he did not even hesitate to face his closest friend in battle for the sake of his cause.

Interested in volunteering to aid others since she was very young, she helped elevate the position of nurses who had long been considered little more than servants through her efforts. id:
As elusive as they are rare, changelings are variously said to be the punishment of indiscretion, the product of supernatural mishap, or even a stolen child of the Fae. Whatever they are, most keep out of sight, and for good reason—unscrupulous humans abduct them as slaves or worse due to their innate talents for illusion and bewitching.

The unfortunate result of a scandalous liaison between a noblewoman and an amorous Fae, Sidonie's ruby sclera was enough to identify her as one of the fair folk, but her appearance too human for her father's people to bear her away to the Vale, rendering her an outcast between two worlds.

Fearing a witch-hunt from her superstitious kinsmen, Sidonie's mother left her in the care of an apothecary, hoping the town's reputation for attracting Eastern traders—a strange folk said to wield magics not unlike the Fae—would help the child escape the bulk of the unwanted attention. Thus did Sidonie spend her formative years among Eastern mystics, but a persistent longing for *something* soon stirred in her heart. It was on her sixteenth birthday that she stole away on a caravan to carve out a niche in a world that seemed to both fear and love her.

Mischievous curiosity was the bedrock for what would be well-remembered lessons in adulthood; after one too many close shaves, Sidonie learned to walk on the wild side. With clever glamours and illusory hexwork, Sidonie's reputation as an excellent infiltrator grew, and a single, star-crossed meeting with a wolf-eyed man would alter her course forever.

But never did Sidonie think she would someday become the key that would entangle both the worlds in a spiral of love and hatred.

id: A Musketeer of righteous and just heart from another world. Many are familiar with the story of his encounter with the heroes known as the Three Musketeers, and how this helped him grow as a person. The words he spoke to display his comradery with the Musketeers in the heat of battle have become the stuff of legend. He was regarded with favor by both ruffians and nobles alike, as this champion of the people is said to have always been fair, even with prisoners.

id:
The illustrious patriarch looked out of his study and into the mist, from which his castle perched upon the moor. Though well past his prime, Leopold was still respected as the undisputed head of House Auswald. A stern and stately man well-versed in both word and swordplay, Leopold placed his hopes in his only son Wulfric, who he hoped would someday lead in his stead.

And yet for all his wisdom, Leopold's keen eyes never saw the betrayal of the Central kingdoms. The men who so easily agreed to Auswald's departure from the ruling houses to found their own empire came by night in silent steel and flickering fire, until all that remained was grieving ash.

The old wolf knew they meant to burn him and his kin in their den. Leopold ordered Wulfric to flee through the underground passage; so long as he lived, the wolves of Auswald would someday return. Death did not take the old patriarch easily; his cane-sword dripped with gore even as he fell unblinking.

Years passed, and Wulfric laid his family standard to rest out of fear of pursuers, eking out a meager existence in the poorer outskirts of the province. Any thought of reclaiming his birthright had long since cooled to mere embers, and it was with a tired sigh that he admonished his son Baelfyr for clamoring after ghost stories.

But the old wolf of Auswald heard the pup's cry, and came to him. It was with great interest that Leopold watched his grandson's zeal flare to life; he had far more courage than his father, and perhaps it was for this reason Leopold sought in him the tool of his vengeance...

Or had it been the boy's sole ambition that had spawned such a phantom?

Death did not take the old patriarch easily; his cane-sword dripped with gore even as he fell unblinking.

Years passed, and Wulfric laid his family standard to rest out of fear of pursuers, eking out a meager existence in the poorer outskirts of the province. Any thought of reclaiming his birthright had long since cooled to mere embers, and it was with a tired sigh that he admonished his son Baelfyr for clamoring after ghost stories.

But the old wolf of Auswald heard the pup's cry, and came to him. It was with great interest that Leopold watched his grandson's zeal flare to life; he had far more courage than his father, and perhaps it was for this reason Leopold sought in him the tool of his vengeance...

Or had it been the boy's sole ambition that had spawned such a phantom?

id:
Deep within the groves the shadows sing for their dusk-mantled master.
A being older than most, bearing an appearance highly contradictory to his true nature, Gwyll is quite literally the stuff of nightmares—so it seems to those foolish enough to cross the Erlking. Indeterminate of gender as the self-styled monarch is, he does not object to being labelled male, perhaps for the ease of those who enter his sunless realm.
Underneath Gwyll's childish facade lies a fickle temperament, as quick to laughter as he is to anger—and certainly as benevolent or vengeful as the moon-kissed tides can be. His unpredictable nature spells a special kind of chaos for those who dare to delve into the depths of unconsciousness, making him something of a spirit, deity, or even demon of the "space." Though scholars disagree on the exact nuances of this plane, most accept that it is a sort of "collective unconscious"—the bedrock of common thought across sentient worlds.
From there the Erlking watches over each and every possible dimension with childlike glee, coveting all but the most precious of souls to pass through. His elfin traits leads to the belief that Gwyll favors the appearance of what some worlds call the "fair folk." Indeed, like them, naive is the one who believes the Erlking is charitable, for even in the abstract there is a price to be paid.
An oft-quoted piece of advice from antiquity still holds: "ware thee the Alder-King, or risk revelry beyond even one's final breath." For as many have claimed to have staggered home from their escapades, many more are found collapsed in their summoning circles as bleached-white bone, with legs worn to mere stumps...

id: The shotguns that Teresa used to punish the wicked had almost no recoil, and could shoot bullets at a terrifying speed. She took out the ruffians of the band she had once belonged with incredible ease, and yet not a single one of their bullets ever managed to hit her—a miracle rewarding her faith. Once Teresa made sure that the young woman wielding the relic guns had won against the false messenger of the gods, she set off on a journey with her. The legends of the "fighting nun" heard of in various regions today are said to have begun around that time.

id:
Horus, future Lord of the Horizons, was born to Aesys and Osiris, first among the ancient pantheon of the land of Urzyma. Conceived shortly before the Lord of Life had left to investigate an unknown disruption in the fabric of reality, Horus never truly knew his father—even before Osiris had been reduced to a twisted shell of his former self by the God-King.

Fearing for her only progeny's life, Aesys sequestered her young son and herself far from the trail of slaughter. She bestowed upon him the name Harakhte, hoping it would help protect him from their pursuers; an infant god's true name was susceptible to scrying magic, and its feeble essence too easily manipulated.

Under Aesys's careful nurture, Harakhte grew into a self-assured youth, possessing his mother's passion and devotion and his father's solemnity. But as the prince grew, so did his curiosity and sense of duty; he wanted so desperately to right the wrongs in the world, and to face the true horror of their sworn enemy.

It was with trepidation and reluctance that Aesys agreed for him to venture outside of their sanctuary, but deep in her heart knew that she too yearned to uncover the truth behind her husband's demise. Harakhte took nightly excursions into the Nameless Capital, serving as her eyes and ears, returning to her each dawn with harrowing tales.

Until the young god saw the twisted nature of fallen Man, and vowed to reclaim the honor of his kin, even as fate struck him down in the blush of youth. Harakhte's spirit persisted, however, and it was the unbending will of a kind priestess that ultimately served as his mortal Vessel.

id: Mariano and his gang had laid two traps for the girl with the gun relic. Once he realized that the assassin sent out to kill the girl as part of his first plan had failed, he took hostage a boy belonging to a tribe of local sanctuary guardians, and then waited for his prey. However, that plan failed as well, and he was ultimately forced to fight her face to face. Although Mariano was quite skilled in combat, he was no match for the girl with the gun relic and her comrades in arms. Following his gang's bitter loss he was arrested by the sheriff, but was able to break free during a scuffle on their way to the county jail. This allowed him to rendezvous with his lover and escape into the sunset.

id:
In an age far removed from dragons and deities, Inara—the name assigned to the subject of this experiment—is truly a legend in living flesh. Reconstructed with mysterious technology analogous to that of other highly-developed worlds, this artificial manifestation of a violent goddess of eld replicates to near-perfect accuracy her power whispered of in serpentine tongues.

It is said that the great corpse in the deepest reaches of what ancient sources called the Endless Abyss harbored within itself lingering life, and it was with this in mind that the researchers selected a biological shell to encourage its growth. All candidates were carefully fielded and systematically erased of personal identity. Whoever this woman was before Inara was of no concern to her keepers.

Inara's sole companion is the loyal serpent Vishap. Though merely a technologically clever approximation of ancient magic, Vishap nevertheless possesses the capability for meaningful thought and speech. Scattered research notes imply he may have been derived from a source said to be extremely close to the original goddess.

For reasons yet undiscovered, the project was abandoned before Inara was able to remember her awakenings, suggesting that she was an induced amnesiac while under stasis in the facility. Upon leaving her cradle for the first time, Inara wrestled with memories false and new flooding her senses.

She would not have to wait long, however, before a certain resonance with an entity beyond the stars would threaten her rule in the realm bequeathed to her. With Vishap's hissing advice in her ears, Inara bided her time in observation of this foolish challenger...

id: When Sheriff Gilbert learned that a young boy from the tribe that protected the mines had been kidnapped by a gang of bandits, his rage shook the heavens. As he and the young girl with the relic gun approached the bandits' hideout, the courage of the young hostage would prove to be the ace up their sleeve that would lead them to victory. After rescuing the young boy the locals who feared Gilbert had a change of heart, making the sheriff's heart swell with pride. Not only did he manage to capture the bandits that attacked his town, he was regarded as a hero and keeper of the peace ever since.

id: Although Carlos had decided to fight against the gang of bandits to protect his home, he ended up being taken hostage by them instead. The bandits demanded that the girl exchange her relic gun for Carlos's life, but unbeknownst to them the young boy had already lit the fuse tied to the explosives he was carrying, ready to die to protect his homeland. The girl prevented an explosion by shooting off the fuse with her gun, but the commotion created by it all left the bandits at a disadvantage. Once the battle ended, Carlos taught his tribe the true meaning of justice, and instilled in them a sense of duty when it comes to protecting their sanctuary.

id:
At languid flame the withered tongues of men
Whispered frightfully a name beyond ken.
But fit the cosmic-shadowed dancer saw
To grant their timeworn audience twilight's fall.

Behold, shattered carapace of mine flesh—
Behold! That which is dead shall live again!

Colors in hues too ill for mortal eyes;
Pulsing static, ichoric, breathless cries—
Echoed thunder, hollow ring: cloudless skies
Could not bear the curse of ancient demise—

And here, I rise. Smoldering with greater vice.

I turn, and burn; there will be nothing left
When I am sated. And all that is, shall rest
In ash and dust. Even time will forget
That once there was love. Hate. Perhaps regret.

Only hunger remains. For I alone
in dim memory recall the last that shone.

The ones before that showed me the way home.

In ash and dust. Even time will forget
That once there was love. Hate. Perhaps regret.

Only hunger remains. For I alone
in dim memory recall the last that shone.

The ones before that showed me the way home.
raw.pt:
At languid flame the withered tongues of men
Whispered frightfully a name beyond ken.
But fit the cosmic-shadowed dancer saw
To grant their timeworn audience twilight's fall.

Behold, shattered carapace of mine flesh—
Behold! That which is dead shall live again!

Colors in hues too ill for mortal eyes;
Pulsing static, ichoric, breathless cries—
Echoed thunder, hollow ring: cloudless skies
Could not bear the curse of ancient demise—

And here, I rise. Smoldering with greater vice.

id:
Inmate ID: XX-13-0
Charges: -
Cell: Solitary Confinement
Notes: Supervise at ALL TIMES.

The 13th Correctional Facility (known as "the Madhouse" to those in the field) carries the notorious reputation of housing the most violent and unrepetent criminals, along with those who aren't "all there" in the head. The last category, of course, is always omitted from official records; no one needs to know about those Especially about one particular prisoner being caged in the bowels of the facility.

Apart from her name, little else is known about Ydra, including why she was brought to the facility in the first place. The young woman is surprisingly lucid and well-read for someone permanently strapped into a straitjacket, and her wide eyes either stare off into space or track her keepers across the room. The supervisor's notes only indicate the time and duration of each session with the facility's therapist, ending abruptly with a redacted entry and no further visitations. Wardens whisper, of course, and talk of devilish giggles and mercurial moods painted Ydra in an unsettling, almost demonically possessed, light.

During the Survivor Games, Ydra had the good fortune (or perhaps Saya had the misfortune) to find an ally of convenience in the chainsaw-wielding felon. Her mind a delicate maze of madness, one can only imagine whether Ydra sees leaving her cage as freedom enough—even if it was still within the locked-down facility. And if the laserblades strapped to her ankles are any indication, this may have been a greater experiment altogether...

id:
Inmate ID: V-1024-52
Charges: Criminal intimidation, aggravated assault
Cell: Level V
Notes: One (1) lethal weapon confiscated — modified chainsaw

A rough-speaking, tomboyish girl incarcerated in the 13th Correctional Facility following what is recorded as a "large public disturbance escalating to manslaughter." Toughened by a life of hardship following a difficult childhood, Saya was no stranger to frequent clashes with authority, which she abhors for their corruption and complacency. However, saying that she dispenses her own personal brand of justice is too noble a statement; everyone knows it's every man, woman, and child for themselves on these streets.

Selfish and suspicious of others, Saya's distrust often leads her to doubt their intentions—a trait that has served her well through the years. While not averse to violence if provoked, she much prefers intimidation tactics—if her swaggering manner won't scare off a thoughtless thug, her massive chainsaw certainly will. No one is quite sure where she acquired such a weapon, though there are many channels through which illegally modified tools end up in the lawless outer city. As Saya puts in her own words: "No one's gonna help you. Talk loudly and carry a huge metal stick. Preferably with metal teeth."

Relucantly drawn into the mysterious—and punishing—Survivor Games at the behest of a mysterious voice over the facility's PA system, Saya's abrasive personality seems like a winning formula for reaching the base floor with the correct key. At least, she believed so, until she met Ydra...

id:
The most stable form of the ascended Sliver known as Kranus, who was originally a mechanical husk housing the madness distilled from Draegar's tortured mind. Owing to the inherent chaos of the Void and the catastrophic end of Prime Athensphere, it was initially erratic, shifting between blinding light and interminable darkness; no doubt this was drawn from the demigods' own beliefs of their creators. However, after an arduous journey forced by circumstance, the Sliver seems to have chosen its light-form permanently.

For every world on the Prime, its divergent twin exists beyond the Veil—an invisible, cosmic curtain that separates the two timelines. While Prime Athensphere met its untimely end when Gazia attempted to seize the power of the Void for himself, its Echo remained intact, though it was not without its troubles—a trait common to all worlds, Echo or no. After observing Azius's attempts to make contact across the vast space, Kranus took matters into its own hands and waited for an opportune moment to spirit the Summoner away. All told, it was a miracle the Summoner arrived safely, though they would later be returned to Grand Gaia by an unexpected third party.

Later, Noel proposed an initiative to observe the Echoes from a safe distance in the Summoner's Hall, and it was clear that the Sliver had made forays of its own elsewhere. Delving deeper into Kranus's mysterious goals, the Summoner's fate became entangled with the Void and its nemesis, the Queen in Cobalt.

No one but the Summoner would know what became of this cosmic rivalry; indeed, some wonder if anything happened at all, or if they had simply failed to remember...

No one but the Summoner would know what became of this cosmic rivalry; indeed, some wonder if anything happened at all, or if they had simply failed to remember...

id: Although Sheena had succeeded thanks to the advice of the Fighting Nun, things turned for the worse when the gang of bandits demanded she traded her relic gun for the life of a boy who had been taken hostage while attempting to protect his home—the sanctuary. Unexpectedly, however, the kidnapped boy caused a distraction that gave Sheena the upper hand once again, allowing the Sheriff, the Fighting Nun, and the hopeful locals to aid her in the fight against the bandits. After rising victorious against the villains, the leader of the gang of bandits challenged Sheena to one last duel. Once the two relic gun wielders faced each other off, only the righteous one would remain standing. Sheena began wielding both relic guns thereafter, leaving many to wonder exactly who she was.

id:
After an untold number of world-hopping adventures and endless acts of derring-do, Tilith had to admit she was past due for a well-deserved break. Even the guardian goddess of humanity needs to recharge! And so it was that Tilith poured all her heart and soul into a wish—and this time, something answered.

Normally, such tales end in comical disaster at best and terrible tragedy at worst, but not for one so pure of heart and sincere intention. Following the burst of light and sound, the gentle caress of sunlight greeted the goddess, and an endless expanse of golden sand stretched out before her.

This was it. This was the fabled Starfall Island she had wanted to visit with her Summoner! Though most would rightly question the exact details of how—and more importantly, why—one could so easily teleport to a destination seen only in the mind's eye, Tilith felt only bliss in that moment; not to mention an overwhelming desire to jump for joy. Legend has it that stars landed on the island to rest, and the stardust left in their wake seeped into the beaches, giving rise to the aptly named "starsand." Unsurprisingly, this has given rise to the idea that the island brims with wish-granting magics.

Soon, Tilith found other people on the island, no doubt here as part of an out-of-season holiday destination. With so many things to do, Tilith set off exploring. Memories are all the sweeter when experienced with friends, whether old or new! Surely there must be many, many memories waiting to be made on this island, and best of all, with her beloved Legendary Summoner...

id:
An awakened Ancient is not to be trifled with, even if she bears the vessel of a young girl.

Once, the Morokai and the Deva were one. Known as the Ancients, they were possessed of incredible power, but the first apocalypse sundered their souls in twain. Long had the powerful Morokai overlord Azurai sought a means to seize this power for himself through the Ritual of Awakening, but it would first require the blood of an awakened Ancient. Thus did he set his sights on young Ezra, born of Morokai and Deva blood. With the assistance of High Inquisitor Aranvis, a trap was laid and sprung, and Ezra fell within their dark grasp.

The Rih'alnase, free-spirited Morokai warriors under the banner of their chieftain Avani, tore a bloody path of rescue toward their young charge alongside her adoptive uncle, the Deva librarian Allanon. By the skin of their teeth and nearly at the cost of Allanon's life, the dark ritual was reversed, but a glimpse of the half-awakened Ancient within Ezra was a nightmare for the ages.

Had the intrepid band failed in their mission, Ezra would have most certainly lost her mind from the influx of uncontrollable power. The awakened Ancient would have then gone on to wreak havoc across all of Eneroth, leaving naught but a trail of destruction in her wake, and not even the famed overlord Azurai could hope to stop her.

All that would remain of their war-torn world would be ash and blood. For their sakes, and perhaps especially for that of the Rih'alnase and Allanon, it was just as well such a fate had not come to pass. Yet such possibilities still resurface in the dark depths of one's mind while walking the straits of traumatic memory...

Once, the Morokai and the Deva were one. Known as the Ancients, they were possessed of incredible power, but the first apocalypse sundered their souls in twain. Long had the powerful Morokai overlord Azurai sought a means to seize this power for himself through the Ritual of Awakening, but it would first require the blood of an awakened Ancient. Thus did he set his sights on young Ezra, born of Morokai and Deva blood. With the assistance of High Inquisitor Aranvis, a trap was laid and sprung, and Ezra fell within their dark grasp.

The Rih'alnase, free-spirited Morokai warriors under the banner of their chieftain Avani, tore a bloody path of rescue toward their young charge alongside her adoptive uncle, the Deva librarian Allanon. By the skin of their teeth and nearly at the cost of Allanon's life, the dark ritual was reversed, but a glimpse of the half-awakened Ancient within Ezra was a nightmare for the ages.

Had the intrepid band failed in their mission, Ezra would have most certainly lost her mind from the influx of uncontrollable power. The awakened Ancient would have then gone on to wreak havoc across all of Eneroth, leaving naught but a trail of destruction in her wake, and not even the famed overlord Azurai could hope to stop her.

All that would remain of their war-torn world would be ash and blood. For their sakes, and perhaps especially for that of the Rih'alnase and Allanon, it was just as well such a fate had not come to pass. Yet such possibilities still resurface in the dark depths of one's mind while walking the straits of traumatic memory...

id: Vanessa inherited her relic gun from her father, and eventually had to face off against a young girl who had a relic gun of her own. The girl preached justice wherever she went, and thus the locals eventually surrounded Vanessa's gang of bandits in search of their own justice. Although Vanessa could've easily left it all behind and fled, her pride was such that she chose to stay behind and fight every single last one of her enemies. Having always manipulated others with fear, she now had to find something scarier than justice itself to gain back control. Thus, she challenged the young girl with the relic gun to a duel—a bullet heard around the world would decide their fate.

id:
Once upon a time, there lived in a little cottage a sweet little girl named Maeri. She wanted not for company (that was what her fluffy friend Woolie was for), but she yearned to go on wonderful adventures like the ones from her stories. Being a small child, however, had its host of difficulties—chief among them getting eaten in one bite by a ravenous bear or some other horrible monster. And there was also the matter of where; Maeri didn't exactly live in a place conducive to wanton acts of derring-do or saving maidens from monsters.

The best Maeri could do was imagine, and how she had a talent for it! For the little girl frequently dozed off during the day, but became lively in the world of dreams. Between the pages of her favorite books pulsed a certain magic— one that brought her above and beyond her comfortable little cottage to snowbound townships and deep, luminous forests.

But to passively observe was a chance wasted. Maeri wanted to be a part of these wonderful tales. Surely the people in the stories wouldn't think much of her; they were not real, after all!

With the narration set firmly in her mind, the young girl set forth. A glittering snowscape unfolded before Maeri's eyes, framed on either side by frosty forests. Deep within the valley nestled an idyllic little village—the first scene. The adventure was about to begin in earnest.

Little did Maeri know, however, how profound an impact she would have in the world she believed was firmly in the realm of relaxed fantasy. For the inhabitants of that snowy world, it was no dream at all...

id:
That the land is alive is a truth all creatures understand, be they beasts of the earth, or men of civilization. To live in harmony was to seek its blessings, and return that which was taken. Such is the cycle of life, and all eventually find their final rest within the earth's bosom, to nurture and nourish its next seeds.

This pure essence of life, however, also births immaterial creatures—spirits. As they grow, they begin to take shape, with many choosing an appearance similar to the denizens of their domain. Glaes walks the earth in the form of a mighty stag, a crystalline core wreathed in verdant foliage and winter blossoms. Rare is the human who catches a glimpse of his majesty; most who do are often starving to death, hopelessly lost in the deepwood, only to be saved by a guiding light.

As one of the older spirits, Glaes shoulders the burden of protecting the land and its inhabitants. He has seen many things in his time—some wrought by man with steel and fire, and others by vicious creatures twisted by their own ambitions. Still, Glaes was rarely moved to violence, and for that he had to thank the sound judgement of the humans in the valley beyond the forest. With his guardianship coming to a close, Glaes retired to the earth.

But shrill cries awakened him once more. A terrible blizzard ravaged the land, resulting in a long and brutal winter, and both man and beast huddled in their dens in despondence.

Shaking off years of inactivity, Glaes pledged himself to finding a solution. First things first: a strange little sheep had wandered far from home and into his forest...

raw.th:
That the land is alive is a truth all creatures understand, be they beasts of the earth, or men of civilization. To live in harmony was to seek its blessings, and return that which was taken. Such is the cycle of life, and all eventually find their final rest within the earth's bosom, to nurture and nourish its next seeds.

This pure essence of life, however, also births immaterial creatures—spirits. As they grow, they begin to take shape, with many choosing an appearance similar to the denizens of their domain. Glaes walks the earth in the form of a mighty stag, a crystalline core wreathed in verdant foliage and winter blossoms. Rare is the human who catches a glimpse of his majesty; most who do are often starving to death, hopelessly lost in the deepwood, only to be saved by a guiding light.

As one of the older spirits, Glaes shoulders the burden of protecting the land and its inhabitants. He has seen many things in his time—some wrought by man with steel and fire, and others by vicious creatures twisted by their own ambitions. id:
Vyrr considered herself rather lenient, refraining from ripping her "opponent" to shreds over his feeble insult. The self-styled hero was nevertheless quivering in his boots, and was barely holding on to the brand-new sword he probably believes is legendary. As her impressive frame cast an imposing shadow over her trembling adversary, his eyes widened even more when she told him—in no uncertain terms—to leave.

"Wait, you're letting me...go?"

Vyrr sighed. Her kin could have at least *tried* to leave a better impression. It was well-known that dragons are proud and terribly dangerous creatures. Many preferred solitude, but some insisted on toying with humans, whether it's snatching maidens or commandeering a castle (both of which are ill-advised). As a result, dragon slayers have risen to fame dispatching the more notorious ones. Even Vyrr had to agree some had it coming, but it didn't help having their entire race condemned.

As for Vyrr, she was more interested in the magical curiosities humans come up with. Showing up at a mage tower as an enormous red dragon, however, was bound to evoke hysterical screaming. So she learned to conceal herself...somewhat. Vanity dictated she would retain her draconic traits, but in time, she came to boast among her visitors a number of learned eccentrics.

Still, a dragon was a dragon, and as winter approached, Vyrr felt the need to hibernate. Tired and sleepy, Vyrr shooed the confused hero out of her cavern, and settled down for another long sleep. The blizzard was oddly harsh this year, but it was nothing her inner flame couldn't keep warm.

After all, who else would be foolish enough to wake a sleeping dragon?

id:
Silently, the owl followed them between the hanging vines. Tall, skittish; bulky, jovial; short, with a temper to match. Luro watched each of the young hunters in turn and smiled to himself. Perhaps it was pride that led them to take the road less traveled, or the misguided notion that untrodden paths lead to greater rewards. Naivety had all but blinded them to the forest's dangers, and before long, they would surely pay the dire price.

A soft hoot echoed through the dark forest, setting off a ripple of tension in the hunting party. The young men exchanged uneasy glances, but they pressed on nonetheless. The fools—there was nothing there but a steep fall. Luro flitted closer and opted for a closer branch this time. His second call drew the attention of the leader, whose face paled at the sight of that blind silver eye.

The floor decided to fall away at that very moment, detritus scattering into the deep void of the hidden cliffs below. With a startled yelp, the bulky man leapt backwards, nearly flattening his smaller companion. In hushed and frightened tones, the men quickly decided to abandon their venture, fleeing under the cold watch of the moon.

Such was the power of Owl's dire omen—for Luro was punished by the Great Spirit, and his call would forever herald misfortune. But none knew the whole truth of it; whether he rejected his own beliefs or buried the truth in the dark nights he inhabits. No one save the strange little girl and her prophetic book.

Luro would have his justice and free himself of those shackles—but was blind to the key in his own hand.

id:
For years, wolves had contended with their competitors in the vast deepwoods they called home: the fire-wielding, silver-steeled creature known as Man. It was through the intervention of the stag spirit Glaes that a tenuous balance was kept, though time and again a brash hunter or a reckless pup would cast this into doubt.

Yet, for her part, so long as they learned to keep their distance from her pack, Kisrai was willing to live and let live.

Known as the Wolf Queen, this enormous white wolf with glowing golden eyes treads the line between myth and reality. Ghostly in appearance, the only indicator of her presence is a haunting howl echoing across the deep ravine. On nights when the full-bellied moon cast its baleful glare across the land, her song was said to sound especially wistful.

But in private, Kisrai had a different side: a stately human woman garbed in fine robes. Such blasphemous revelations, however, were mere curiosities when presented to scholars who fraternize with a dragon. Shapeshifting, to them, was more academically rigorous than the product of fevered hearsay. Shifters had long existed in their world, hiding beneath shaded boughs and whispering brooks, but those whose livelihood depended on the earth preferred their folktales.

As for the true identity of the Wolf Queen, none could say. No noblewoman or court mage matching her description had vanished from the public eye, and to willingly relinquish such a position of privilege was preposterous. Still, the stole Kisrai wears upon her shoulders bears striking similarity to the famed companion of a legendary sorcerer long deceased...

Yet, for her part, so long as they learned to keep their distance from her pack, Kisrai was willing to live and let live.

Known as the Wolf Queen, this enormous white wolf with glowing golden eyes treads the line between myth and reality. Ghostly in appearance, the only indicator of her presence is a haunting howl echoing across the deep ravine. On nights when the full-bellied moon cast its baleful glare across the land, her song was said to sound especially wistful.

But in private, Kisrai had a different side: a stately human woman garbed in fine robes. Such blasphemous revelations, however, were mere curiosities when presented to scholars who fraternize with a dragon. Shapeshifting, to them, was more academically rigorous than the product of fevered hearsay. Shifters had long existed in their world, hiding beneath shaded boughs and whispering brooks, but those whose livelihood depended on the earth preferred their folktales.

As for the true identity of the Wolf Queen, none could say. No noblewoman or court mage matching her description had vanished from the public eye, and to willingly relinquish such a position of privilege was preposterous. Still, the stole Kisrai wears upon her shoulders bears striking similarity to the famed companion of a legendary sorcerer long deceased...

id:
Full of vigor and larger than life, this young beast and his outlandish mannerisms stand out like a sore thumb in a land of sullen snow and ice. Ni'en, as he called himself, belonged to a race of fantastically strange creatures known as Sanje from beyond the sea. Sporting golden manes flowing over a body encased in emerald scales, fiery eyes, and ruby-red antlers above the brow, their brutish appearances led many to label them misshapen monstrosities.

None of that discouraged Ni'en from seeking out company, however. Inherent to intelligent creatures were "spirits", the pure energies of life. Good spirits kept a Sanje happy, while they would devour the impure ones. Though Ni'en invoked transformative magics to conceal his beastly appearance, part of his face and one arm escaped unchanged. Far from being bothered, Ni'en figured it was pretty "cool", as he heard human youth describing the concept to each other. And if started conversations, so much the better!

Unfortunately, after getting run out of every village, Ni'en started to feel disheartened. Why were humans so difficult to understand?

As he wandered farther into the wilds, something in the distance piqued his senses, along with the familiar scent of scorched earth. Kin? In these forsaken lands? But beneath the burns smoldered something strange, something dark...and Ni'en had a mind to follow his intuition. Cracking his knuckles (gently, with his human hand!), the spirited youth huffed out a breath and followed in their wake.

For however grotesque Ni'en may seem, none knew better than he when there was evil to be devoured.

id:
Hailing from a distant land of curious magecraft, Guinne's magic-weaving of choice is almost literal—'threads' of energy control puppets known as weavedolls, resulting in a visually distinct manner reminiscent of traditional marionettistes.

As ethereal beings of immaterial form, lesser spirits can manifest both in flesh or in a material vessel. The most common ones are crystal, but the greater the spirit, the purer a crystal must be, and those often command prices far beyond the reach of a humble mage.

For weavedolls, simply connecting threads of energy to their limbs is sufficient, but it comes with the caveat of manual control—a price to pay for complete obedience over the more haphazard free-spirits. In search of greater autonomy and sentience without breaking the bank, Guinne struck west.

After months of research into what precious few scraps of information she could glean from smuggled manuscripts from a distinguished scholar's library, Guinne finally pieced together what she deemed a viable solution. The weavedolls could make do with crystal shards, and by channeling her will into a more powerful spirit—a servitor or 'shadow'—the greater spirit could command its lessers, circumventing the need for multiple expensive cores. All that was left was the matter of the servitor's own vessel, for which her research concluded was to be the summoner themselves.

Steeling herself, Guinne invoked the dangerous ritual, setting up as many failsafes as she could muster. But through her concentration, stray desires clung to the purity of her intentions and coalesced into a most alluring form...

As ethereal beings of immaterial form, lesser spirits can manifest both in flesh or in a material vessel. The most common ones are crystal, but the greater the spirit, the purer a crystal must be, and those often command prices far beyond the reach of a humble mage.

For weavedolls, simply connecting threads of energy to their limbs is sufficient, but it comes with the caveat of manual control—a price to pay for complete obedience over the more haphazard free-spirits. In search of greater autonomy and sentience without breaking the bank, Guinne struck west.

After months of research into what precious few scraps of information she could glean from smuggled manuscripts from a distinguished scholar's library, Guinne finally pieced together what she deemed a viable solution. The weavedolls could make do with crystal shards, and by channeling her will into a more powerful spirit—a servitor or 'shadow'—the greater spirit could command its lessers, circumventing the need for multiple expensive cores. All that was left was the matter of the servitor's own vessel, for which her research concluded was to be the summoner themselves.

Steeling herself, Guinne invoked the dangerous ritual, setting up as many failsafes as she could muster. But through her concentration, stray desires clung to the purity of her intentions and coalesced into a most alluring form...

id:
Long ago, an eccentric scholar uncovered the nature of Desire, culminating in a tome possessing the power to control one's destiny. Following his mysterious decline and death, few—if any—returned from his ruinous tomb. But while his magnum opus may have been lost, the art of binding spirits was not. The scholar's own servant, a devilish woman of surpassing beauty and guile, entertained visitors during the scholar's life. The envy of many, she was possessed of individual will yet obedient to her master's every command—a powerful servitor spirit, far outranking the humble familiars most mages had.

Methods and manuals smuggled out of the scholar's library were disseminated by disgruntled acquaintances, and soon, the secret of such a pact was revealed: servitors desired an exchange of equal value, relative to their would-be master.

Nabris was drawn to the desperate invocations of a mage from a distant land. As a spirit of desire, he was especially attuned to emotions, specifically those which lurked in the darkest corners of the summoner's heart. His physical appearance cast in the image of such thoughts, it was with wicked glee that he greeted his flustered mistress. But to his dismay, her instructions were rather less than...thrilling, to say the least.

Bored out of his mind and playing guardian to a host of minor spirits beneath his concern, Nabris decided it was past time for a display of arcane power. He could taste the deepest yearnings in his mistress's mind; let he be the one to give voice to them, and show her the true face of her soul...

id:
Born into nouveau riche, Phaedra's house was never truly considered by the nobles as one of their kind. Though the sight of their ilk elicited casual disdain from their snobbish elite peers, her parents strove to provide her with the best education money can buy; after all, Phaedra was their only hope in rising up the social ladder.

While they busied themselves hobnobbing with the upper crust of society, the first embers of revolution were being stoked. The Wolf's Eyes—armed visionaries led by a power-hungry man named Baelfyr—whipped the masses into a frenzied bloodlust. Talk of retribution against the Vale over the Starsage's corruption spurred conscription, including Phaedra's bodyguard, a rugged and loyal man named Angahl.

Fearing that the kingdom was no longer safe, Phaedra's parents sent her in the guise of a new recruit to seek Angahl out at the forward camp. Once there was a lull in the fighting, he would secret her away to the countryside. But when the injured arrived in droves, Phaedra was immediately called upon as a medic, and she never saw her guardian.

Deep in the midst of conflict, Phaedra was rescuing the stranded in the Vale when she was struck by a burst of Fae magic. Blinded and reeling from pain, Phaedra still pressed on, offering as much aid as she could until exertion overwhelmed her. When she next awoke, the world was awash in a veil of white—including her memories.

It seemed that something important was taken from her, but what? A few friendly spirit-like entities accompanied her quiet recuperation in this gentle clearing, but all she had to go on was a carved flower emblem...

id:
A fiercely loyal retainer of a minor house in the kingdom, Angahl had humble beginnings as the eldest son in a peasant family of five. Robust and healthy since childhood, his size and strength made him ideal for manual labor. A traveling noble and his entourage chanced to witness the lad's impressive feat of wrestling a ferocious boar to the ground, and offered to hire him as a bodyguard with the promise of a better life.

Angahl grew to be a stoic man of few words, but displayed surprising gentleness toward his charge, the young lady Phaedra. His brooding demeanor frightened the girl at times, however, and Angahl soon learned to keep his watch at a distance. Nevertheless, a silent friendship blossomed between the two, and he would come to consider himself her stalwart guardian.

When Baelfyr and his Wolf's Eyes ordered an assault on the Vale, Angahl received a missive from his lord to secret Phaedra away once she arrived at the forward camp in the guise of a new recruit. Soon after, a violent confrontation exploded into ceaseless fighting, and Angahl was deployed to the frontlines as a mobile shield. His penchant for holding any line earned him the epithet 'unbreakable', but none would predict the Wolf's Eyes turning on them instead.

Left at the mercy of the enraged elementals, Angahl broke ranks to rescue Phaedra in the chaos, and that was the last anyone would ever see of him. Some say the earth howled with vengeance and swallowed men whole that day; others insist he was truly unbreakable, and to this day wanders the ruins a haunted shell of a man, forever in search of his missing charge...

id:
Working on the frontlines of urban defence is rough, and that goes double if you happen to be a Volper, an elite among the Rezcorps guardsmen of Paskua's most technologically advanced military organization. You have to possess a keen sense of danger, a thick skull for impact, and above all, an appetite for controlled destruction. Despite the harsh requirements, Buck seems to be enjoying his career, or else he wouldn't have stayed this long.

A former instructor in the academy, Buck was well placed to dispense his grizzled advice to fresh-fraced, overeager cadets. Many who enter Rezcorps dream of joining the ranks of the prestigious Volpers, but only a few make the cut each year, and for good reason. It's not enough to simply be a good guardsmen; the Volpers put their lives on the line for the people they lead and serve.

Having seen his fair share of trials and tribulations throughout the years, Buck's stories are etched into his skin, each scar and burn a memory of a mission completed or a civilian rescued. Then there were those he could not save, but such grim realities come with the job; Buck would rather laugh it off over a pint than brood himself into oblivion.

Buck currently partners with Lleva, a rising young boltstriker within the Volpers whose stoic and serious demeanor complements his laid-back calmness. The pair had met before; Buck oversaw her training at one point, alongside a second promising cadet named Bonnie.

Who knew that years later, both of his trainees would come to walk their own paths and be reunited over a certain diabolical genius?

id:
Forming the elite of the technologically advanced military organization known as Rezcorps, Volpers are deployed in pairs along with a small squadron of rank-and-file guardsmen to neutralize threats within the urban landscapes of Paskua.

A rising star among their ranks, Lleva has the honor of being one of the most talented boltstrikers on the force. The boltblade she wields channels ambient static in the air and concentrates them into an electric burst capable of stunning or short circuiting mechanical opponents—an ideal counter against renegade robots, the preferred minions of urban threats.

It might have been a grim coincidence that Lleva and her partner Buck were assigned to oversee the interrogation of Vikki, a self-proclaimed "evil genius" who was able to send one of her lackeys to another world. It seemed like only yesterday when Lleva was just a cadet in the academy along her friend and rival Bonnie when they had heard of a talented mind within the field of robotics...

Now, as she stood stoic before the heavy lamp, Lleva almost felt sorry for the slight figure on the other side of the table—save for Vikki's self-satisfied grin. There was a job to be done, and Lleva prided herself on completing any mission set out for her. That was why she succeeded where Bonnie had left; Bonnie who was always too much of a firebrand. Bonnie, who had visited Vikki before disappearing.

Clearing her throat, Lleva began the interrogation. She would get to the bottom of this mysterious business, and when she finally pulled Bonnie out of what was certain to be some harebrained scheme, she would have choice words for her.

id:
Among Giselle's many odd talents, one stands head and shoulders above the rest—creating culinary delights the likes of which none in the known universe has ever seen before...or probably would want to, for that matter.

Every Summoner that has had the dubious fortune to taste her cooking and has somehow lived to tell the tale speak of visions and experiences straight out of a madman's fevered dream. From technicolor tentacles slithering along the length of a cavernous floor to the steely glint of an unblinking eye set in the hilt of her knife, watching Giselle work her magic is like delving deeply into one of Grand Gaia's most enduring secrets regarding its alien visitor, and to embrace madness itself.

...Or is the experience highly subjective and personal? To the outside observer, the friendly administrator of the Orebus Special Inquiry only seems to be an amateur chef bustling over a few pots, pans, and powders. Surely, if Giselle's form had begun unravelling into a cosmic horror as she served up another helping of her strange stew, everyone at the Summoner's Guild would have noticed by now.

In any case, you find yourself seated at the small wooden table. Giselle brandishes her curiously clean knife with a flourish and sets the bubbling bowl before you. What was that warning you heard from the wide-eyed Summoner you passed in the hall again?

Your attention is brought back to Giselle's smiling face as she beams at you.

"Bon appetit, darling! ...And try not to mind the wiggling!"
name: MST_UNITCOMMENT_811038_DESCRIPTION
desc:
Among Giselle's many odd talents, one stands head and shoulders above the rest—creating culinary delights the likes of which none in the known universe has ever seen before...or probably would want to, for that matter.

Every Summoner that has had the dubious fortune to taste her cooking and has somehow lived to tell the tale speak of visions and experiences straight out of a madman's fevered dream.
